Read out of saint.gr's line for 23 Ιουλίου, «Άγιος Απολλινάριος επίσκοπος Ραβέννας», with the rank word and the see left off. The page's own distich spells the name «Aπολινάριον», with one lambda.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 23. јул ст. ст., „Свештеномученик Аполинарије.“ — «Свештеномученик» is the rank, written out in full on this day where most of this book’s headings abbreviate it, and §6 leaves it off. **The heading is that one word and the name, and nothing else at all**, so the bare forename is the whole of the form; the see is in `office` and the «of Ravenna» of the display name is the corpus’s own. `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` and `sr-foldpred.mjs` `new key, other holders: 0 (none)`.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 23 iulie — «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Apolinarie, episcopul Ravenei»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 23ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιος Απολλινάριος επίσκοπος Ραβέννας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 23 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the man is the folder's own: the disciple and follower of the apostle Peter, whom he followed from Antioch to Rome and who ordained him bishop of Ravenna. He is not `apollinaris-mosalitinov`, the twentieth-century Russian monk-martyr. The Greek page adds the names the Romanian source did not: Boniface, a distinguished man of Ravenna, deaf and dumb, whom he healed, and his daughter who had a demon; the patrician Rufinus in Aemilia whose daughter he raised; the shipwreck that put him ashore in Moesia of Thrace; the Christian centurion who let him go from prison; and the seven days he lived after the beating that disfigured him. Its distich sets him beside the day's other Ravenna saint — «Tον Aπολινάριον εκτετμημένον, Έσπευσε Bιτάλιος αυτίκα φθάσαι» — and the corpus keeps that Vitalis as `vitalis-the-martyr-23-july`, upgraded on this same day; the page does not say the two knew each other, so no `related` row is proposed. It gives no year anywhere, so no `dates` are proposed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 05.08.2026 (23. јул ст. ст.) — „Свештеномученик Аполинарије.“

attestations.note: The day’s second and last entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop (§4). «Свештеномученик» is the `hieromartyr` this folder already carries by §5; `bishop` beside it is not in the heading and is left alone, though the body states it outright — „Ученик апостола Петра, родом од града Антиохије. Св. Петар га узе собом из Антиохије у Рим, и у Риму га рукоположи за епископа града Равене.“, the apostle Peter took him out of Antioch to Rome and there **ordained him bishop of the city of Ravenna**, which is also the `Bishop of Ravenna` the folder already has in `office`, confirmed here from a third book. **The heading is one word and a name and there is nothing else in it at all.** **`dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THE FIELD IS AND STAYS ABSENT, WHICH COSTS SOMETHING HERE.** This folder has no `dates` object. **This entry gives no year either, and it offers three things that are not years.** It names the emperor Веспазијан, who answered the heathen elders’ letter; it makes him a disciple of the apostle Peter; and it counts two spans, **twelve years in the commander’s house and three years of work in the Balkans**. A reign is not a date, an apostle is not a date, and a span with no point to hang it from is not a date — the same three refusals the twenty-seven years of Ezekiel and the two ages of Cornelius took on the two days before. Nothing is written. **NO FOLD.** `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Аполинарије» and `sr-foldpred.mjs` `new key, other holders: 0 (none)`. It is the only form of this day that lands in no fold. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, AND IT IS A WHOLE MISSIONARY CAREER THIS FOLDER DID NOT HAVE. „Дошавши у Равену Аполинарије уђе у дом некога војника Иринеја, коме исцели сина од слепила, и кроз то обрати цео дом вери Христовој.“ — at Ravenna he went into the house of a soldier Иринеј, **healed his son of blindness** and turned the whole house; „Исто тако исцели од неког тешког недуга и жену војеначалника Равенског, те и његов сав дом крсти.“, he healed the wife of the commander of Ravenna and baptised all his house; „По жељи војеначалника Аполинарије оста у његовом дому на становању. Ту направи и једну домаћу цркву. И пребиваше у том дому 12 година, проповедајући Јеванђеље и крштавајући неверне.“, he stayed in that house at the commander’s wish, **made a house church in it** and remained there twelve years preaching and baptising. „Од незнабожачких старешина би љуто мучен у више махова, но свесилна десница Божја подржа га и спасе га.“, he was cruelly tortured more than once by the heathen elders and the right hand of God upheld him. Then **the exile and the shipwreck**: „Најзад би осуђен на прогонство у Илирик (на Балкан).“, condemned to banishment to Illyricum — **«на Балкан», to the Balkans, which is the book’s own gloss on the old province and the clearest mark of who wrote it** — and „Но лађа, на којој путоваху, разби се од буре и потону, и одсвих путника спасе се само св. Аполинарије са два војника и три клирика своја.“, the ship broken by a storm and sunk, and of all the passengers only Apollinaris saved, with two soldiers and three of his clergy; „Чудесно тако спасени војници повероваше у силу Бога Аполинаријевог и крстише се.“, and the soldiers so saved believed and were baptised. „Тада Аполинарије пође проповедати Јеванђеље по целом Балкану, спуштајући се до Дунава. По том се упути у Тракију, где такође под притиском великим шираше Јеванђеље Господње.“ — **then he preached over the whole of the Balkans, coming down as far as the DANUBE, and then into THRACE** — and „После 3 године рада на Балкану би протеран натраг у Италију. Он дође у Равену, где му се сви верни необично обрадоваше.“, after three years of that work he was driven back to Italy and came to Ravenna, where all the faithful rejoiced beyond measure. **AND THEN THE EMPEROR’S ANSWER, WHICH IS FORTY-FOUR WORDS AND THE BEST THING ON THE PAGE.** „Чувши за ово старешине незнабожачке писаху цару Веспазијану о Аполинарију као мађионичару, и питаху га да ли да га предаду смрти као непријатеља њихових богова.“, the heathen elders wrote to Vespasian about him **as a magician** and asked whether to put him to death as an enemy of their gods; and „На то цар одговори, да га не треба убијати него само тражити да принесе жртву боговима, или да се из града изагна, јер вели: „не приличи се да се светимо некоме за богове, јер они сами могу се осветити непријатељима својим, ако се прогњеве.““ — the emperor answered that he should not be killed but only required to sacrifice, or else driven out of the city, **for it is not fitting that we should avenge anyone for the gods, since they can avenge themselves on their own enemies if they are angered.** A pagan emperor’s argument against persecution, quoted by a bishop in a Serbian prologue. „Но и мимо ове царске наредбе незнабошци ударише на Аполинарија и ножевима га избодоше. Од тешких рана овај слуга Божји издахну и пресели се у царство Божје.“, the heathen went against even that order, set on him and stabbed him with knives, and of the heavy wounds he breathed out; „Мошти св. Аполинарија почивају у Равени, у цркви његовог имена.“, his relics rest at Ravenna in the church of his name. **ONE `related` ROW, BOTH WAYS, WHERE THE FOLDER HAD NONE AT ALL.** This folder’s `related` was `null`. The entry makes him **the apostle Peter’s own disciple, taken by Peter from Antioch to Rome and ordained by Peter**, which is as plain a relation as a book states, so `peter-the-apostle` goes on in both directions and is linked in the prose. `proseprobe.mjs` over the drafted paragraph returned **`0 name(s) the index would link`** — `peter-the-apostle`’s display name is not the bare «Peter» the prose uses — so `related-floor.test.mjs` demanded nothing; **the row is owed instead by `life-links.test.mjs`, because the prose LINKS him**, and the reverse row is supplied because the relation is real and not because a test asked. **THE SOLDIER Иринеј GETS NOTHING ON RULING 3**: `ls saints | grep -i irenaeus` returns several folders and not one is a soldier of Ravenna whose blind son Apollinaris healed. The commander of Ravenna and his wife are named by no name at all; the two soldiers and three clergy of the wreck likewise; the emperor Vespasian is no saint and holds no folder. **THE CHURCH OF HIS NAME AT RAVENNA IS A DEDICATION** and a dedication is not a relation. No `locations`: Antioch, Rome, Ravenna, Illyricum, the Balkans, the Danube, Thrace and Italy are eight places in one entry and not one is written as a coordinate. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only Bishop Nikolai’s verse.
